errors.text_span: The figure illustrates a comparison of attention scores across different layers for various gating configurations in a large language model, focusing on the presence of massive activations and attention sinks.
errors.evidence: This sentence provides an interpretation based on external context (likely the paper's caption) that is not visible in the figure itself. The figure displays data for a single configuration ('atten_output_gate_head_share'), not a 'comparison' of 'various gating configurations'.

The description fails to state the specific purpose of the chart as indicated by its title: 'first token attention score of atten_output_gate_head_share'. Instead, it provides a generalized and incorrect purpose.
The description states the score at layer 20 is 'around 0.04', but the chart shows the value is approximately 0.08.
The description claims the score is 'stabilizing' near layer 22, but the chart shows a continued steep decline from approximately 0.08 at layer 20 to below 0.02 at layer 22.
The description states the score at layer 22 is 'near 0.04', but the chart shows the value is much lower, at approximately 0.02.
The description states the crossing of the mean line occurs 'around layer 5.5', but the chart shows this crossing happens before layer 5.

The description omits the full title of the chart, which is "first token attention score of atten_output_gate_head_share". This additional context, present in the reference description, clarifies what specific metric is being plotted.
The description states that the x-axis (layer number) ranges from 0 to 22. However, the plotted data extends to layer 23.

The description claims the blue line remains above the mean from layer 6 to layer 17. According to the graph, the line is above the mean for a wider interval, from approximately layer 5 to layer 19. This significantly misrepresents the duration of the period where attention scores are above the mean.
